li.span: To easily rebuild the hardlink folder for the bad installs or expired rebuild and then just symlink to correct package
To easily manage all the version of same package

div.span: Why cant pnpm directly hardlink in the main node_modules folder for all the packages: -

li.span: Hardlinking the files for every packages will also require hardlinking the files for the nested dependencies too, and because hardlinking can only be done for files and not folder this would slower the file system process

text.tspan: Why cant pnpm directly hardlink in the main node_modules folder
for all the packages: -
Hardlinking the files for every packages will also require
hardlinking the files for the nested dependencies too, and because
hardlinking can only be done for files and not folder this would
slower the file system process

ol.li: pnpm creates a hidden folder inside our project node modules -> node_modules/.pnpm. This is called virtual store This is here the actual contents live. one subfolder per exact package version (for all dependencies, devdependencies and even for nested dependencies etc)

For each package version, pnpm reads the package's index files and every entry, Hardlinks the corresponding content hash file from store/v11/files/xx/... into the node_modules/.pnpm/packageNmae@version

li.span: Now pnpm links the top-level dependencies in our project main node_modules via symlinks
Nested/transitive dependencies also symlink to its respective hardLinked folder created in node_modules/.pnpm

text.tspan: pnpm creates a hidden folder inside our project node modules
-> node_modules/.pnpm. This is called virtual store This is here
the actual contents live. one subfolder per exact package
version (for all dependencies, devdependencies and even for
nested dependencies etc)For each package version, pnpm
reads the package's index files and every entry, Hardlinks the
corresponding content hash file from store/v11/files/xx/... into
the node_modules/.pnpm/packageNmae@versionNow pnpm
links the top-level dependencies in our project main
node_modules via symlinksNested/transitive dependencies also
symlink to its respective hardLinked folder created in

ol.li: All the local projects that use the pnpm and for globally installed packages, pnpm creates a symlinked reference file, in its project folder in pnpm directory
Each folder name in this project folder is a hash of their absolute path. (check by calculating sha-256 hash of the folder absolute path, before runing pnpm add cmd)
Now when we run prune cmd, pnpm always checks this directory, for the check unreferenced/orphan packages, instead of scanning the whole operating system fies
every time we run pnpm install/pnpm add cmd in any project, it get registered in this project directory

span.span: Run the pnpm prune cmd and notice the number of packages it is checking, and then count the number of projects in the project folder of pnpm directory

div.div:
1. pnpm uses a content-addressable store. Files are stored according to a hash of their contents
The hash is alway calcuated for the files in a package while adding in store, now even if two package have same content, their hash will always be same

text.tspan: 1. pnpm uses a content-addressable store. Files are stored according
to a hash of their contents
The hash is alway calcuated for the files in a package while adding in
store, now even if two package have same content, their hash will
always be same

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 380px; height: 1px; padding-top: 881px; margin-left: 1391px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; max-height: 196px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.div: FIles are stores in hash-based sharding/fan-out architecture: -

span.style: scrollbar-color: rgb(75, 75, 75) rgb(27, 29, 30); color: light-dark(rgb(192, 192, 192), rgb(255, 255, 255));

li.span: const hash = "00cc06fe80fe136b07a2bcc082944..."; // just computed from file bytes of a file

span.style: scrollbar-color: rgb(75, 75, 75) rgb(27, 29, 30); color: light-dark(rgb(192, 192, 192), rgb(255, 255, 255));

li.span: const dirName = hash.slice(0, 2); // "00" <- This file will go in this directory

span.style: scrollbar-color: rgb(75, 75, 75) rgb(27, 29, 30); color: light-dark(rgb(192, 192, 192), rgb(255, 255, 255));

li.span: const fileName = hash.slice(2); // rest of hash will be the name of that file

span.style: scrollbar-color: rgb(75, 75, 75) rgb(27, 29, 30); color: light-dark(rgb(192, 192, 192), rgb(255, 255, 255));

li.span: const fullPath = `store/v11/files/00/cc06fe80fe136b07a2bcc082944...`; // And it will be stored like this, So the full file hash is calculated as dir Hash + file Hash

text.tspan: FIles are stores in hash-based sharding/fan-out architecture: -
const hash = "00cc06fe80fe136b07a2bcc082944..."; // just computed
from file bytes of a fileconst dirName = hash.slice(0, 2); // "00" <- This
file will go in this directoryconst fileName = hash.slice(2); // rest of hash
will be the name of that fileconst fullPath =
`store/v11/files/00/cc06fe80fe136b07a2bcc082944...`; // And it will be
stored like this, So the full file hash is calculated as dir Hash + file Hash

display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: This way filesystem is optimized, else it would make filesystem lookups slower

span.span: if it does not exist then
Downloads the package in virtual directory, inside a folder named as package name
All the versions of that package will be downloaded in this folder with each package folder named as package version
2. Now pnpm will create hardlinked -> symlinked folders for that package in it cache folder named as the hash computed of the pnpmx cmd content
pnpm does this so that it know the dlx package is also being referenced somewhere
3. Bydefualt dlx packags expiry time is indefinite, if expiry is not configed in config file

div.div: pnpm still has to download the tarball from the registry (npm registry doesn't let you fetch individual files from a package). It always downloads and unpacks the full tarball into memory/temp. But when it's time to write files into the store / link them into node_modules, that's where the dedup kicks in — unchanged files skip the write-to-disk step and just get relinked, and the actual node_modules population is hardlinks either way, not copies. So the savings are mainly in disk space and node_modules population speed, not network bandwidth (there are some registry-level tricks for reducing download size too, but that's separate from the store's content-addressing).

li.span: Before downloading: pnpm fetches the metadata of the package from the npm registry. This metadata includes the hash in data.integrity field
Now pnpm check if any package with that same hash already exists in index.db, If yes then skip downloading that package tarball and reuse that
If no, then pnpm downloads package tarball and calculates the tarball hash to verify integrity.
On success verificaiton pnpm then calculates the hashes of the files in that package to organize the content-addressable store.

text.tspan: Before downloading: pnpm fetches the metadata of the package
from the npm registry. This metadata includes the hash in
data.integrity fieldNow pnpm check if any package with that same
hash already exists in index.db, If yes then skip downloading that
package tarball and reuse thatIf no, then pnpm downloads
package tarball and calculates the tarball hash to verify
integrity.On success verificaiton pnpm then calculates the hashes
of the files in that package to organize the content-addressable
store.
